title: Out on Bail, He Sold Met Gala Tickets That Didn't Exist
hook: Out on bail.|Selling the Met Gala.

lines.say: July two thousand seventeen. Charged over Fyre Festival, Billy McFarland is released on bail.
lines.show: July 2017. Charged over Fyre Festival, Billy McFarland is released on bail.

lines.say: By late that year, prosecutors said, he ran NYC VIP Access, selling tickets to the Met Gala, Coachella, the Grammys, the Super Bowl.
lines.show: By late that year, prosecutors said, he ran NYC VIP Access, selling tickets to the Met Gala, Coachella, the Grammys, the Super Bowl.

lines.say: The Met Gala pitch went out from an employee's email account. Two thousand five hundred dollars a ticket.
lines.show: The Met Gala pitch went out from an employee's email account. $2,500 a ticket.

lines.say: When one buyer wanted proof, he admitted, he created a fake email from the gala's host. No buyer was on the guest list.
Some were Fyre Festival guests. At least thirty customers lost about one hundred fifty thousand dollars.
lines.show: Some were Fyre Festival guests. At least 30 customers lost about $150,000.

lines.say: His bail was revoked. At sentencing, the judge called him unique in the court's memory.

scene.q: Mr. McFarland is unique in this Court's memory.

lines.say: Real trials. Real evidence. The verdict.
